a: If status, obtain the status. If cleanup, clean up the async job cache (by default in ~/.ansible_async/) for the specified job jid.

The DSC configuration document to set or test. See https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/dsc/concepts/configuration-documents/overview?view for an overview of how to author a configuration document.

Path to DSC configuration document either on the control node or the target host. The remote_config_file parameter controls whether the file is located on the control node (false) or the target host (true).
Runtime parameter values. This corresponds to the --parameters commandline option.
Whether the provided config_file is already on the target host. If false, the file will be transferred from the control node to the target host and removed after the module is done.
Specify level of tracing output, which are returned in stderr_lines. This corresponds to the --trace-level DSC commandline option.

a: Path used for local ansible facts (*.ps1 or *.json) - files in this dir will be run (if a ps1) or read (if a json) and their results be added to the return facts.

Set the default timeout in seconds for individual fact gathering.
The file on the remote system to fetch. This must be a file, not a directory.

The rights/permissions that are to be allowed/denied for the specified user or group for the item at path.

User or Group to add specified rights to act on src file/folder or registry key.
Follow the symlinks and junctions to apply the ACLs to the target instead of the link.

Specify whether to add present or remove absent the specified access rule.

a: Path to be used for changing inheritance Support for registry keys have been added in ansible.windows>

Specify whether to enable present or disable absent ACL inheritance.
The type of event you would like to audit for. Accepts a list. See examples.
Single string value for the category you would like to adjust the policy on. Cannot be used with subcategory. You must define one or the other.
Single string value for the subcategory you would like to adjust the policy on. Cannot be used with category. You must define one or the other.

The user or group to adjust rules for.
Defines whether to log on failure, success, or both. To log both define as comma separated list "Success, Failure".
Defines what objects inside of a folder or registry key will inherit the settings. If you are setting a rule on a file, this value has to be changed to none.
Propagation flag on the audit rules. This value is ignored when the path type is a file.

Whether the rule should be present or absent. For absent, only path, user, and state are required. Specifying absent will remove all rules matching the defined user.

a: The number of times to do an automatic logon. This count is deremented by Windows everytime an automatic logon is performed. Once the count reaches 0 then the automatic logon process is disabled.
Password to be used for automatic login. Must be set when state. Value of this input will be used as password for username.
Whether the registry key should be present or absent.

Username to login automatically. Must be set when state. This can be the Netlogon or UPN of a domain account and is automatically parsed to the DefaultUserName and DefaultDomainName registry properties.

a: A list of capability names to add or remove. Supports wildcard patterns like ? for single character matching and * for multiple character matching.
If true, prevents DISM from contacting Windows Update for the source files.

Sets the maximum output level for DISM logging. 0 logs errors only 1 logs errors and warnings 2 logs errors, warnings, and information 3 logs all of the previous plus debug output, only valid on Windows 11 or Server…
Specifies the full path and file name to log to. If not specified the logging uses the default DISM log file location which is %WINDIR%\\Logs\\Dism\\dism.log.
Use the specified locations as capability sources.
Whether the capability should be present or absent. If present, the capability will be added if it is not already present. If absent, the capability will be removed if it is present.
If true, prevents DISM from contacting Windows Update for the source files.
Sets the maximum output level for DISM logging. 0 logs errors only 1 logs errors and warnings 2 logs errors, warnings, and information 3 logs all of the previous plus debug output.
Specifies the full path and file name to log to. If not specified the logging uses the default DISM log file location which is %WINDIR%\\Logs\\Dism\\dism.log.
A list of capability names to filter by. Supports wildcard patterns like ? for single character matching and * for multiple character matching. If not specified, all capabilities will be returned.
Finds capabilities that are available in the specified source locations.
The location of the store to search.
The name of the store to search. See https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.security.cryptography.x509certificates.storename for a list of built-in store names.
The thumbprint as a hex string of a certificate to find. When specified, filters the certificates return value to a single certificate See the examples for how to format the thumbprint.

a: The file type to export the certificate as when state. der is a binary ASN.1 encoded file. pem is a base64 encoded file of a der file in the OpenSSL form.
Whether to allow the private key to be exported. If false, then this module and other process will only be able to export the certificate and the private key cannot be exported. Used when state only.
Specifies where Windows will store the private key when it is imported. When set to default, the default option as set by Windows is used, typically user.
The password of the pkcs12 certificate key. This is used when reading a pkcs12 certificate file or the password to set when state and file_type.
The path to a certificate file. This is required when state is present or exported. When state is absent and thumbprint is not specified, the thumbprint is derived from the certificate at this path.
If present, will ensure that the certificate at path is imported into the certificate store specified.
The store location to use when importing a certificate or searching for a certificate. Can be set to CurrentUser or LocalMachine when store_type. Defaults to LocalMachine when store_type.
The store name to use when importing a certificate or searching for a certificate.
The store type to manage. Use system to manage locations in the system store, LocalMachine and CurrentUser. Use service to manage the store of a service account specified by store_location.
The thumbprint as a hex string to either export or remove. See the examples for how to specify the thumbprint.
The win_command module takes a free form command to run. This is mutually exclusive with the cmd and argv options. There is no parameter actually named '_raw_params'. See the examples!
A list that contains the executable and arguments to run. The module will attempt to quote the arguments specified based on the Win32 C command-line argument rules.
Set the specified path as the current working directory before executing a command.
The command and arguments to run. This is mutually exclusive with the _raw_params and argv options.
A path or path filter pattern; when the referenced path exists on the target host, the task will be skipped.

This option overrides the encoding of stdout/stderr output. You can use this option when you need to run a command which ignore the console's codepage. You should only need to use this option in very rare circumstances.
A path or path filter pattern; when the referenced path does not exist on the target host, the task will be skipped.
Set the stdin of the command directly to the specified value.

a: String value to apply to Windows descripton. Specify value of "" to clear the value.
String value of organization that the Windows is licensed to. Specify value of "" to clear the value.
String value of the persona that the Windows is licensed to. Specify value of "" to clear the value.
ansible.windows.win_computer_description.d: Set windows description, owner and organization

a: Remote path where the file should be copied to. If the path is not absolute, the path will be relative to the current working directory of the module process.
Determine whether a backup should be created. When set to true, create a backup file including the timestamp information so you can get the original file back if you somehow clobbered it incorrectly.

When used instead of src, sets the contents of a file directly to the specified value. This is for simple values, for anything complex or with formatting please switch to the ansible.windows.win_template module.
This option controls the autodecryption of source files using vault.
If set to true, the file will only be transferred if the content is different than destination. If set to false, the file will only be transferred if the destination does not exist.
This flag indicates that filesystem links in the source tree, if they exist, should be followed.
If false, it will search for src at originating/controller machine. If true, it will go to the remote/target machine for the src.
Local path to a file to copy to the remote server; can be absolute or relative. If path is a directory, it is copied (including the source folder name) recursively to dest.
ansible.windows.win_copy.d: Copies files to remote locations on windows hosts

a: The target that identifies the server or servers that the credential is to be used for.
The type of credential to store. This is used with name to produce a unique credential. When the type is a domain type, the credential is used by Microsoft authentication packages like Negotiate.
Adds an alias for the credential. Typically this is the NetBIOS name of a host if name is set to the DNS name.
A user defined comment for the credential.
Defines the persistence of the credential. If local, the credential will persist for all logons of the same user on the same host.
The secret for the credential. When omitted, then no secret is used for the credential if a new credentials is created. When type is a password type, this is the password for username.
Controls the input type for secret. If text, secret is a text string that is UTF-16LE encoded to bytes. If base64, secret is a base64 string that is base64 decoded to bytes.
When absent, the credential specified by name and type is removed. When present, the credential specified by name and type is added.
When always, the secret will always be updated if they differ. When on_create, the secret will only be checked/updated when it is first created.
When type is a password type, then this is the username to store for the credential. When type is a credential type, then this is the thumbprint as a hex string of the certificate to use.
The key for the attribute. This is not a unique identifier as multiple attributes can have the same key.
Controls the input type for data. If text, data is a text string that is UTF-16LE encoded to bytes. If base64, data is a base64 string that is base64 decoded to bytes.

ansible.windows.win_credential.d: Manages Windows Credentials in the Credential Manager

a: Specifies a DHCP server. You can specify an IP address or any value that resolves to an IP address, such as a fully qualified domain name (FQDN), host name, or NETBIOS name.
Specifies the description for reservation being created. Only applicable to l(type=reservation).
Specifies the DNS hostname of the client for which the IP address lease is to be added.
Indicates the type of DNS record to be registered by the DHCP. server service for this lease. l(a) results in an A record being registered. l(aptr) results in both A and PTR records to be registered.

Specifies the duration of the DHCP lease in days. The duration value only applies to l(type=lease). Defaults to the duration specified by the DHCP server configuration. Only applicable to l(type=lease).
The IPv4 address of the client server/computer. This is a required parameter, if l(mac) is not set. Can be used to identify an existing lease/reservation, instead of l(mac).
Specifies the client identifier to be set on the IPv4 address. This is a required parameter, if l(ip) is not set. Windows clients use the MAC address as the client ID.
Specifies the name of the reservation being created. Only applicable to l(type=reservation).
Specifies the scope identifier as defined by the DHCP server. This is a required parameter, if l(state=present) and the reservation or lease doesn't already exist.
Specifies the desired state of the DHCP lease or reservation.
The type of DHCP address. Leases expire as defined by l(duration). When l(duration) is not specified, the server default is used. Reservations are permanent.
Adapter name or list of adapter names for which to manage DNS settings ('*' is supported as a wildcard value).
Single or ordered list of DNS servers (IPv4 and IPv6 addresses) to configure for lookup.
Specifies a list of global suffixes that can be used in the specified order by the DNS client for resolving the IP address.
ansible.windows.win_dns_client.d: Configures DNS lookup on Windows hosts

a: The type of DNS record to manage. SRV was added in the 1.0.0 release of this collection. NS was added in the 1.1.0 release of this collection. TXT was added in the 1.6.0 release of this collection.
The name of the zone to manage (eg example.com). The zone must already exist.
Should aging be activated for the record. If set to false, the record will be static.
Specifies if any authenticated user can update the record. If set to true, any authenticated user can update the record.
Specifies a DNS server. You can specify an IP address or any value that resolves to an IP address, such as a fully qualified domain name (FQDN), host name, or NETBIOS name.
The port number of the record. Required when type. Supported only for type.
The priority number for each service in SRV record. Required when type. Supported only for type.
Whether the record should exist or not.

The "time to live" of the record, in seconds. Ignored when state. Valid range is 1 - 31557600. Note that an Active Directory forest can specify a minimum TTL, and will dynamically "round up" other values to that minimum.
The value(s) to specify. Required when state. When type only the partial part of the IP should be given. Multiple values can be passed when type
Weightage given to each service record in SRV record. Required when type. Supported only for type.
The name of the zone scope to manage (eg ScopeAZ). The zone must already exist.
Fully qualified name of the DNS zone.
Specifies the name of an existing custom Active Directory application directory partition where the zone should be stored.

Specifies an list of IP addresses of the primary servers of the zone. DNS queries for a forwarded zone are sent to primary servers. Required if l(type=secondary), l(type=forwarder) or l(type=stub), otherwise ignored.

Specifies how a zone handles dynamic updates. Secure DNS updates are available only for Active Directory-integrated zones. When not specified during new zone creation, Windows will default this to l(none).
Specifies a length of time, in seconds, that a DNS server waits for a remote DNS server to resolve a query. Accepts integer values between 0 and 15.
Specifies the replication scope for the DNS zone. l(replication=forest) will replicate the DNS zone to all domain controllers in the Active Directory forest.
Specifies the desired state of the DNS zone. When l(state=present) the module will attempt to create the specified DNS zone if it does not already exist.
Specifies the type of DNS zone. When l(type=secondary), the DNS server will immediately attempt to perform a zone transfer from the servers in this list.
The ansible.windows.win_dsc module takes in multiple free form options based on the DSC resource being invoked by resource_name. There is no option actually named free_form so see the examples.
The name of the DSC Resource to use. Must be accessible to PowerShell using any of the default paths.
Can be used to configure the exact version of the DSC resource to be invoked. Useful if the target node has multiple versions installed of the module containing the DSC resource.
The level at which to set the environment variable. Use machine to set for all users. Use user to set for the current user that ansible is connected as. Use process to set for the current process.
The name of the environment variable. Required when state.
Set to present to ensure environment variable is set. Set to absent to ensure it is removed. When using variables, do not set this option.
The value to store in the environment variable. Must be set when state and cannot be an empty string. Should be omitted for state and variables.

A dictionary where multiple environment variables can be defined at once. Not valid when state is set. Variables with a value will be set (present) and variables with an empty value will be unset (absent).
ansible.windows.win_environment.d: Modify environment variables on windows hosts

a: Name of the event log to manage.
For one or more sources specified, the path to a custom category resource file.
The maximum size of the event log. Value must be between 64KB and 4GB, and divisible by 64KB. Size can be specified in KB, MB or GB (e.g. 128KB, 16MB, 2.5GB).
For one or more sources specified, the path to a custom event message resource file.

The action for the log to take once it reaches its maximum size. For DoNotOverwrite, all existing entries are kept and new entries are not retained. For OverwriteAsNeeded, each new entry overwrites the oldest entry.
For one or more sources specified, the path to a custom parameter resource file.
The minimum number of days event entries must remain in the log. This option is only used when overflow_action is OverwriteOlder.
A list of one or more sources to ensure are present/absent in the log. When category_file, message_file and/or parameter_file are specified, these values are applied across all sources.
Desired state of the log and/or sources. When sources is populated, state is checked for sources. When sources is not populated, state is checked for the specified log itself.
Names of roles or features to install as a single feature or a comma-separated list of features. To list all available features use the PowerShell command Get-WindowsFeature.
Adds the corresponding management tools to the specified feature. Not supported in Windows 2008 R2 and will be ignored.
Adds all subfeatures of the specified feature.
Specify a source to install the feature from. Not supported in Windows 2008 R2 and will be ignored. Can either be {driveletter}:\sources\sxs or \\{IP}\share\sources\sxs.
State of the features or roles on the system.
ansible.windows.win_feature.d: Installs and uninstalls Windows Features on Windows Server

a: If specified, this is used to match the name of the Windows feature to get the info for. Can be a wildcard to match multiple features but the wildcard will only be matched on the name of the feature.
Path to the file being managed.
The desired access time for the file or directory. A DateTime string in the format specified by access_time_format. The timestamp is interpreted as local time on the target system.
The format to use when parsing access_time. Defaults to yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss. See .NET DateTime format strings.
The desired modification time for the file or directory. A DateTime string in the format specified by modification_time_format. The timestamp is interpreted as local time on the target system.
The format to use when parsing modification_time. Defaults to yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss. See .NET DateTime format strings.

If directory, all immediate subdirectories will be created if they do not exist. If file, the file will NOT be created if it does not exist, see the ansible.windows.win_copy or ansible.windows.win_template module if you…

a: The full path of the file or directory to modify. The path must exist on file system that supports compression like NTFS.
This option only has an effect when recurse is true If true, will check the compressed state of all subdirectories and files and make a change if any are different from compressed.
Whether to recursively apply changes to all subdirectories and files. This option only has an effect when path is a directory. When set to false, only applies changes to path.
Set to present to ensure the path is compressed. Set to absent to ensure the path is not compressed.
ansible.windows.win_file_compression.d: Alters the compression of files and directories on NTFS partitions.

a: List of paths of directories to search for files or folders in. This can be supplied as a single path or a list of paths.
Select files or folders whose age is equal to or greater than the specified time. Use a negative age to find files equal to or less than the specified time.
Choose the file property against which we compare age. The default attribute we compare with is the last modification time.
Make case-sensitive string comparisons for the filename match. Set use_regex to true to make this work.
Algorithm to determine the checksum of a file. Will throw an error if the host is unable to use specified algorithm.
Set the maximum number of levels to descend into. Setting recurse to false will override this value, which is effectively depth 1. Default depth is unlimited.
Type of file to search for. Specify any to find both file and directory. Added in version 3.2.0.
Set this to true to follow symlinks in the path. This needs to be used in conjunction with recurse.
Whether to return a checksum of the file in the return info (default sha1), use checksum_algorithm to change from the default.
Set this to include hidden files or folders.
One or more (powershell or regex) patterns to compare filenames with. The type of pattern matching is controlled by use_regex option.
Will recursively descend into the directory looking for files or folders.
Select files or folders whose size is equal to or greater than the specified size. Use a negative value to find files equal to or less than the specified size.
Will set patterns to run as a regex check if set to true.

a: Set state of firewall for given profile.
Set to allow or block inbound network traffic in the profile. not_configured is valid when configuring a GPO.
Set to allow or block inbound network traffic in the profile. not_configured is valid when configuring a GPO.
Specify one or more profiles to change.

a: The location to save the file at the URL. Be sure to include a filename and extension as appropriate.
The full URL of a file to download.

Specifies the hashing algorithm used when calculating the checksum of the remote and destination file.
Specifies a URL that contains the checksum values for the resource at url. Like checksum, this is used to verify the integrity of the remote transfer. This option cannot be set with checksum.

The path to the client certificate (.pfx) that is used for X509 authentication. This path can either be the path to the pfx on the filesystem or the PowerShell certificate path Cert:\CurrentUser\My\<thumbprint>.
The password for client_cert if the cert is password protected.
Whether the module should follow redirects. all will follow all redirects. none will not follow any redirect.

If true, will download the file every time and replace the file if the contents change. If false, will only download the file if it does not exist or the remote file has been modified more recently than the local file.
By default the authentication header is only sent when a webservice responses to an initial request with a 401 status. Since some basic auth services do not properly send a 401, logins will fail.
Extra headers to set on the request. This should be a dictionary where the key is the header name and the value is the value for that header.
Header to identify as, generally appears in web server logs. This is set to the User-Agent header on a HTTP request.
Specify how many times the module will redirect a connection to an alternative URI before the connection fails.
An explicit proxy to use for the request. By default, the request will use the IE defined proxy unless use_proxy is set to no.
Uses the current user's credentials when authenticating with a proxy host protected with NTLM, Kerberos, or Negotiate authentication.
The username to use for proxy authentication.
The HTTP Method of the request.
Specifies how long the request can be pending before it times out (in seconds). Set to 0 to specify an infinite timeout.
The username to use for authentication.
Uses the current user's credentials when authenticating with a server protected with NTLM, Kerberos, or Negotiate authentication.
If no, it will not use the proxy defined in IE for the current user.
If no, SSL certificates will not be validated. This should only be used on personally controlled sites using self-signed certificates.

a: Description of the group. Set to an empty string "" to unset the description.
The members to add to the group. This will add the members without removing any existing members not listed.
The members to remove. This will remove the members from the group without removing any existing members not listed.
The members to set the group to. This will replace the existing membership with the users provided in this value. Can be set to [] to clear all members from the group.
A list of members to ensure are present/absent from the group. Accepts local users as .\username, and SERVERNAME\username. Accepts domain users and groups as DOMAIN\username and username@DOMAIN.
Name of the local group to manage membership on.
Desired state of the members in the group. When state is pure, only the members specified will exist, and all other existing members not specified are removed.
The hostname to set for the computer.
Controls the behavior of aliases. Only applicable when state. If add, each alias in aliases will be added to the host entry.
A list of additional names (cname records) for the host entry. Only applicable when state.
A canonical name for the host entry. required for state.
The ip address for the host entry. Can be either IPv4 (A record) or IPv6 (AAAA record). Required for state.
Whether the entry should be present or absent. If only canonical_name is provided when state, then all hosts entries with the canonical name of canonical_name will be removed.

a: The name of the hotfix as shown in DISM, see examples for details. This or hotfix_kb MUST be set when state.

The path to the downloaded hotfix .msu file. This MUST be set if state and MUST be a .msu hotfix file.
Whether to install or uninstall the hotfix. When present, source MUST be set. When absent, hotfix_identifier or hotfix_kb MUST be set.
A list of hosts that will bypass the set proxy when being accessed. Use <local> to match hostnames that are not fully qualified domain names.

A string or dict that specifies the proxy to be set. If setting a string, should be in the form hostname, hostname:port, or protocol. If the port is undefined, the default port for the protocol in use is used.
Instead of manually specifying the proxy and/or bypass, set this to import the proxy from a set source like Internet Explorer.
The URL of a proxy configuration script. Proxy configuration scripts are typically JavaScript files with the .pac extension that implement the FindProxyForURL(url function.

Whether to configure WinINet to automatically detect proxy settings through Web Proxy Auto-Detection WPAD. This corresponds to the checkbox Automatically detect settings in the connection settings window.
A list of hosts that will bypass the set proxy when being accessed. Use <local> to match hostnames that are not fully qualified domain names.

The name of the IE connection to set the proxy settings for. These are the connections under the Dial-up and Virtual Private Network header in the IE settings. When omitted, the default LAN connection is used.

A string or dict that specifies the proxy to be set. If setting a string, should be in the form hostname, hostname:port, or protocol. If the port is undefined, the default port for the protocol in use is used.

a: The letter of the network path to map to. This letter must not already be in use with Windows.

The password for username that is used when testing the initial connection. This is never saved with a mapped drive, use the ansible.windows.win_credential module to persist a username and password for a host.
The UNC path to map the drive to. If pointing to a WebDAV location this must still be in a UNC path in the format \\hostname\path and not a URL, see examples for more details.
If present will ensure the mapped drive exists. If absent will ensure the mapped drive does not exist.
The username that is used when testing the initial connection. This is never saved with a mapped drive, the ansible.windows.win_credential module to persist a username and password for a host.
